data.body:
SCOPE HOLD (operator judgement, 2026-08-19): change 1919 EXCEEDS the authorized scope of this
ticket. The change has been marked WIP in Gerrit so no session can submit it while this is resolved.

This ticket authorized an ADVISORY PROJECT CRITERION. The approved design was explicitly
project-owned — the criterion, its prompt and its evals live in `.rebar/` precisely so no shipped
module carries the project's invariant. The change delivers that, but also carries ~145 lines of
CORE behaviour change plus a new shipped public config key.

IN SCOPE (project-owned, as designed):
  .rebar/criteria_routing.json                       +21
  .rebar/prompts/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.md   +68
  .rebar/evals/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.eval.yaml  +158
  .gitignore                                          +2

OUT OF SCOPE (shipped code and public surface):
  src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py              +85   new project_applies_to_globs /
                                                           criterion_matches_changed_files
  src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py            +22/-9 CHANGES DISPATCH SEMANTICS FOR EVERY
                                                           project code-review criterion, not just
                                                           the new one
  src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py                  +18   new pointer shape-validation
  src/rebar/_config_schema.py / _config_sections.py / config.py   new `[code_review] ci_config_globs`
  tests/golden/config_surface.json                          public config surface changes
  docs/config.md / docs/env-vars.md / docs/llm-framework.md

WHY THIS MATTERS beyond bookkeeping. The gate_dispatch change is a real semantic change with its own
blast radius: activated project code-review criteria were previously injected unconditionally, and
now a glob-gated criterion that matches no changed file is DROPPED. That alters behaviour for
`project.review-phase-boundaries` too (it is spared only because its `applies_to` is empty) and for
any project criterion any downstream project has defined. That deserves its own review, its own
tests, and its own revert unit — not to ride in on an advisory criterion. It is also what pushed
`src/rebar/config.py` to exactly the 800-line cap (see `erratic-illhumored-norwayrat`).

The implementing agent was not wrong that the seam fix was REQUIRED — `applies_to` genuinely had no
effect on project criteria, so the approved portable design was unimplementable without it. The
error was continuing through that discovery inside one change instead of stopping to split it.

RECOMMENDED REMEDY (stacked, per CONTRIBUTING.md §4): two changes, seam first.
  1. "Make applies_to actually gate project code-review criteria" — registry.py, gate_dispatch.py,
     overlay.py + their tests. A standalone core fix, reviewable on its own merits, with the
     unconditional-injection defect as its stated motivation.
  2. This ticket's criterion — `.rebar/` content, the ci_config_globs key and docs — rebased on (1).
Nothing is discarded; the work is re-partitioned so each half is independently reviewable and
revertible. Awaiting operator direction before executing.
